question: The most reliable intraoperative sign that uterine perforation has occurred during D&C is that an instrument (dilator or curette) advances beyond the expected uterine cavity depth without resistance, and the sounding depth is then confirmed to have been exceeded.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The key sign of perforation during D&C is an instrument passing beyond the expected cavity depth without the normal resistance of the uterine fundus. This statement is accurate — memorise this as the most important complication to watch for during observation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Loss of resistance with an instrument advancing beyond the expected cavity depth is the classic sign of perforation. The surgeon will immediately stop instrumentation, assess the patient's haemodynamic status, and decide on laparoscopic inspection or conservative management.
